params.label: Max walking slope
params.note: Lunar-derived NASA suit requirement; Mars value not established.
params.source: NASA EVA-EXP-0042 xEVA System ConOps / Artemis suit requirements (via NTRS 20210000827)

params.label: Never-enter slope (side-hill)
params.note: Cells steeper than this are impassable in any direction.

params.label: Planning walking speed
params.note: 2 km/h on fairly level regolith; slope and soil slow it further.

params.label: Solar-storm rule: max time to shelter
params.note: Derived from 16 surface SEP events seen by Curiosity/RAD: stay within 30 min of shelter.
params.source: Nowcasting SEP events for Mars missions, arXiv 2502.02469

params.label: O2 reserve required on arrival
params.note: 8 h EVA + 1 h secondary oxygen.

params.label: Loose sand: extra travel time
params.note: Time multiplier (1 + k * sand likelihood). Sand layer is an image-based proxy.
params.source: Team model; Pandolf terrain factor for loose sand = 2.1 (Soule & Goldman 1972)

params.label: Astronaut + suit mass
params.note: 80 kg crew member + ~120 kg suit and life support.

params.label: Suit cooling limit
params.note: About 2,000 BTU/h for the Apollo suit and the EMU: heat, not oxygen, caps speed.

params.label: Heat storage: performance drops
params.note: 480 BTU of stored body heat.

params.label: Heat storage: tissue damage
params.note: 800 BTU of stored body heat, treated as mission failure.

params.label: Nominal suited pace
params.note: Apollo 16 long traverses: 0.61-0.91 m/s.

params.label: Brisk pace toward shelter (solar storm)
params.note: Pace the scripted crew uses under a shelter-rule deadline (reference baseline action).

params.label: Fastest pace (walk-run limit)
params.note: Froude number about 0.5 at Mars gravity.

params.label: Metabolic model: M = a + b*v + c*v^2 (a)
params.note: With b = 240, c = 110: 0.65 m/s gives 322 W (Apollo walking: 230-350 W).
params.source: Team fit to Apollo metabolic data (Waligora 1975 via NTRS 20220004017)

params.label: Fall rate on easy ground
params.note: Apollo crews fell 27 times, but no distance denominator exists; rate rises with slope, roughness and speed squared.

params.label: Chance a fall is incapacitating
params.note: Suit damage or injury needing buddy rescue; grows with speed and downhill. Apollo: 27 falls, none incapacitating.

params.label: Rockfall reach angle
params.note: Energy-line angle from source to stop. Lower = boulders travel farther = wider keep-out band.
params.source: Grindrod et al. 2021 (Terra Sirenum, Mars): H/V 1.44-1.90

params.label: Rockfall source slope
params.note: Cells at least this steep can release boulders (>30 deg in the Artemis hazard study; RSL bedrock 35.5 +/- 9.9 deg).

params.label: Boulders released by the marsquake
params.note: Count of new boulder tracks after marsquake S0235b at Cerberus Fossae, not at Melas.

params.label: Post-quake rockfall rate vs. background
params.note: 27 tracks observed where about 2.6 were expected (Cerberus Fossae).

params.label: Post-quake hold on runout band
params.note: Design rule: no entry into the band until the hold expires. No Mars aftershock decay law exists.

params.label: Background dose rate (GCR)
params.note: 0.210 +/- 0.040 mGy/day at Gale crater.

params.label: Quality factor, background (GCR)
params.note: 0.64 mSv/day dose equivalent over 0.21 mGy/day absorbed at Gale crater.

params.label: Quality factor, solar particles
params.note: Proton-dominated event; used to report dose in mSv.

params.label: Solar storm: onset to peak
params.note: Largest surface event on record, 20 May 2024 (Curiosity/RAD).

params.label: Solar storm: unshielded total dose
params.note: NASA/JPL estimate, derived from the RAD data, of the dose an astronaut next to Curiosity would have received on 20 May 2024; not a measurement (RAD itself recorded 1730.55 uGy, Loewe Table 1). Used as the scripted storm's size. Time profile is idealised (linear rise, exponential decay).

params.label: Solar storm: decay time
params.note: e-folding time after the peak.

params.label: Solar storm: alert threshold above background
params.note: The on-site rule raises the alert when the dose rate is this far above the background. Threshold of the published RAD nowcast; the engine applies it to its modelled dose rate.

params.label: Terrain shielding per blocked sky
params.note: RAD at Murray Buttes: 19% of sky blocked gives 12% less downward dose. Cliffs help a little.
params.source: Guo et al. 2021 (RAD beside Murray Buttes)

params.label: Pressurized rover shielding
params.note: Fraction of dose removed inside the rover.

params.label: Habitat storm-shelter shielding
params.note: Fraction of dose removed inside the storm shelter.

params.label: Natural shelter: min. blocked sky
params.note: Terrain cells that hide at least this fraction of the sky are offered as stop-gap shelters.

params.label: Habitat antenna height
params.note: Height above the ground of the habitat radio mast, for the line-of-sight layer.

params.label: Rover antenna height
params.note: Height above the ground of the rover antenna, for the line-of-sight layer.

params.label: Suit antenna height
params.note: Height above the ground of the antenna on a suit backpack.

params.label: Alert to first step
params.note: Time between the alert and the crew starting to walk; counted against the shelter rule.

params.label: Stored heat at the start of the incident
params.note: Crew has been working at the science site.

params.label: Usable O2 at the start of the incident
params.note: About 1.6 h into an 8 h + 1 h EVA.

params.label: Unmapped-terrain slowdown amplitude
params.note: Smooth 40 m value noise slows the walker by up to this fraction (reference sim.ts).

params.label: Navigation error vanishes within
params.note: The crew recognises the shelter in the final stretch, so the navigation offset fades out.

params.label: Dust optical depth (sensor value)
params.note: Daily mean dust column visible optical depth for the site in this season (Ls 22); no dust storm in this scenario.
params.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario, point query at lat -10.01, lon -69.96 E

params.label: Local preview: walkers per route
params.note: Small Monte Carlo run by the engine when no offline stress-test results are present.

params.label: Disturbance: suit cooling multiplier per sigma
params.note: Multiplier 1 - 0.117 z, z clipped to +/-3, floor 0.65 (380 W): SWME without sweep gas.

params.label: Disturbance: metabolic efficiency log-sigma
params.note: Multiplier exp(0.12 z): x0.70 to x1.43.

params.label: Disturbance: navigation error sigma
params.note: 3 sigma = 160 m, the JETT3 mean position error.

params.label: Disturbance: pace drift log-sigma per step
params.note: About +/-13% pace variation (ICES-2026-127).

kinds.measured: Measured on Mars or in tests
kinds.model: Model output or estimate (team or published), not a measurement
kinds.scenario: Scripted for the demo, not an observation
